edges.description: Reproduces the human biallelic truncating genotype in human cardiomyocytes with an isogenic control, which is the allelic configuration this node describes.
edges.limitations: This is a resource report. It establishes pluripotency, karyotype and three-germ-layer plus cardiomyocyte differentiation, and reports no cMyBP-C protein quantification and no disease phenotype, so it substantiates the genotype arm of this node and not the protein-depletion arm. hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes are also fetal-like and two-dimensional, with no ventricular wall in which compaction could be assessed.

edges.description: Establishes the transcript-level fate of MYBPC3 premature termination codon alleles in human cardiomyocytes: no truncated peptide, and chronic nonsense-mediated decay activation.
edges.limitations: The lines are heterozygous, the CMH4 allelic regime, not the biallelic regime that defines LVNC10, so the dose state this node turns on is not the one modeled. More pointedly, protein levels were comparable to isogenic controls despite reduced mRNA, which the authors read as haploinsufficiency not contributing in vitro. That does not overturn the ~20% residual protein measured in affected human cardiac tissue in a compound heterozygous LVNC case, but it does mean this model supports the transcript arm of the node and not the protein-depletion arm.

edges.description: The homozygous null genotype reproduces the allelic state the biallelic human genotype produces, and the paper makes the mono- versus bi-allelic dose contrast explicitly.
edges.limitations: Neither the cited abstract nor this entry has a residual-protein figure for the mouse, so "near-complete depletion" is inferred from the null genotype rather than measured; the readout available is gross cardiac enlargement, an organ-level proxy standing in for a molecular node. The mouse also survives to adulthood, where the equivalent human genotype is fatal within months.
edges.target: MYBPC3 Loss-of-Function Variant and cMyBP-C Depletion

edges.description: The model reproduces the allelic dose and the neonatal timing of the human compaction phenotype, and supplies a cellular mechanism - failure of postnatal myocyte cell-cycle exit - that could plausibly divert ventricular wall maturation. It does not reproduce the noncompaction phenotype itself.
edges.limitations: The mouse phenotype is cardiac dilation with myocyte hyperplasia, not a persistently hypertrabeculated, noncompacted ventricular wall; the abstract reports no trabecular-to-compact remodeling measurement. Homozygous null mice also survive into adulthood, where the human biallelic genotype is lethal within months. Treating the cytokinesis finding as the explanation of human compaction failure is an inference the cited work does not make.

edges.description: Neonatal AAV-U7-AON treatment prevented the cardiac dysfunction and hypertrophy that this homozygous Mybpc3 genotype otherwise produces, establishing the neonatal window as a point of intervention on the organ-level failure node.
edges.limitations: The rescued phenotype is hypertrophy with cardiac dysfunction, not noncompaction, so the experiment shows that a biallelic Mybpc3 cardiac phenotype is correctable rather than that the human LVNC10 compaction defect specifically is. The authors also report the effect as transient and requiring optimization, and the construct is exon-6-specific, so it would not transfer to the human truncating alleles curated in this entry without redesign.

edges.description: Perinatal death with cardiac disease reproduces the lethal timing of the human biallelic phenotype in a large animal.
edges.limitations: The reported cardiac phenotype is hypertrophy; no noncompaction, hypertrabeculation, or septal defect is described. Only a single edited MYBPC3 piglet is reported, and cloning by somatic cell nuclear transfer independently causes perinatal loss, so the death cannot be attributed to the genotype alone. The authors' own conclusion is that pigs are unusually sensitive to sarcomeric variants, which is itself a caution against reading the timing across to humans.

edges.description: Homozygous knockout of the cMyBP-C orthologue reproduces the protein-loss state and yields cardiomyocyte hyperplasia, matching the murine null.
edges.limitations: The zebrafish heart is two-chambered and the gene is an orthologue rather than human MYBPC3, so the model speaks to conserved cMyBP-C cell biology and not to human ventricular architecture. Its wall phenotype runs opposite to the human one: the mutant ventricle is more compact and thicker-walled, not hypertrabeculated.
edges.target: MYBPC3 Loss-of-Function Variant and cMyBP-C Depletion

edges.description: Controlled re-expression of wild-type cMyBP-C on the null background recovered ventricular function, showing the phenotype tracks the current protein level rather than a fixed consequence of having lacked it.
edges.limitations: The reversibility demonstrated is of the adult contractile and hypertrophic phenotype. LVNC10's defining lesion is a developmental failure of ventricular compaction laid down before birth, and nothing in this model tests whether that is reversible; a compaction defect could well be fixed even where contractile function is not. Knockdown was also partial rather than complete.

nodes.description: When cMyBP-C is reduced to a small fraction of normal by biallelic truncating (or loss-of-function-plus-missense) MYBPC3 genotypes, the fetal myocardium fails to complete the normal trabecular-to-compact remodeling process, leaving a persistently noncompacted, hypertrabeculated ventricular wall. The precise molecular step by which near-complete cMyBP-C loss diverts the myocardium toward a noncompaction phenotype, rather than toward the hypertrophic remodeling seen with partial (monoallelic) haploinsufficiency in CMH4, is not established (see the discussion below).

nodes.description: The homozygous cMyBP-C-deficient mouse is the murine counterpart of the biallelic MYBPC3 allelic state that defines LVNC10, and is the only model in this entry that offers a candidate mechanism for the dose-phenotype divergence recorded in the open discussion below. These mice enlarge their hearts almost twofold shortly after birth, and the enlargement is driven by myocyte hyperplasia rather than hypertrophy: cMyBP-C-null myocytes complete an extra round of postnatal cell division and accumulate as supernumerary mononuclear cells, whereas the heterozygous state produces hypertrophy through increased cell size. The authors propose that cMyBP-C normally acts as an inhibitor of postnatal myocyte cytokinesis, so that near-complete loss releases a proliferative program at exactly the window in which the mammalian ventricle is finishing its trabecular-to-compact remodeling.

nodes.description: Isogenic human cardiomyocytes carrying MYBPC3 premature termination codon variants, including p.R943x - the same nonsense change as the c.2827C>T (p.Arg943*) Dutch founder allele that appears homozygously and in compound heterozygosity in the founding LVNC10 case series. The system establishes two things this entry's molecular node asserts: no truncated peptide is produced, and nonsense-mediated decay is chronically engaged. It also supplies a genuine complication, recorded in the discussion below: at the heterozygous dose in this in vitro system, MYBPC3 mRNA fell but cMyBP-C protein did not.

nodes.description: MYBPC3 encodes cardiac myosin-binding protein C (cMyBP-C), a thick-filament accessory protein of the sarcomeric A band. As in CMH4, most MYBPC3 disease alleles are truncating (frameshift, nonsense, or splice variants), the truncated peptide is not stably detected in patient myocardium, and the operative consequence is reduced functional cMyBP-C protein rather than a dominant-negative poison peptide (see kb/disorders/Hypertrophic_Cardiomyopathy_4.yaml for the detailed nonsense-mediated-decay/proteasomal-degradation mechanism, which is shared with this entry). What differs in LVNC10 is allelic dose: a single truncating allele produces the classic CMH4 haploinsufficiency state (roughly 50% residual protein), while two loss-of-function alleles, or a loss-of-function allele combined with a destabilizing missense allele on the second copy, can reduce residual cMyBP-C to as little as ~20% of normal.

nodes.description: An independently reported compound heterozygous genotype: a loss-of-function MYBPC3 allele combined in trans with a de novo missense variant on the second allele. The missense allele was associated with an unstable protein product, reducing overall residual cMyBP-C to approximately 20% of control levels in affected cardiac tissue, and produced a severe early-onset noncompaction phenotype that required heart transplantation. The reporting study also recommends considering copy-number variants as an additional route to the same biallelic-dose mechanism, though no specific CNV genotype is documented for this MYBPC3 case in the cited literature.

nodes.description: A homozygous Mybpc3 knock-in mouse carrying a single point mutation that generates three aberrant mRNAs, developed as a hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy model but genotypically in the biallelic regime this entry curates. It is included here for the therapeutic arm: AAV-delivered U7snRNA antisense constructs that mask splicing enhancers in exons 5 and 6 shifted splicing toward a functional variant and, injected in newborns, abolished cardiac dysfunction and prevented hypertrophy. This is the only demonstration in this entry that a biallelic Mybpc3 cardiac phenotype is preventable if the protein deficit is corrected in the neonatal window.

nodes.description:
A stable zebrafish knockout of the cMyBP-C orthologue, built as a hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy model but carrying the finding that matters most to this entry: immunofluorescence shows significant cardiomyocyte hyperplasia in mutant hearts at the larval stage (608 vs 302 total cardiomyocyte nuclei), with myocardial remodeling and hyperplasia persisting into later larval development. That is the same cellular response the homozygous cMyBP-C-deficient mouse shows, reached independently in a teleost, which is the strongest support this entry carries for treating hyperplasia as a conserved consequence of cMyBP-C loss rather than a murine idiosyncrasy.
The direction of the wall phenotype is the point to keep hold of. Zebrafish do form a compact ventricular myocardium over a trabecular layer, and this knockout does not fail to compact it - the mutant ventricle and atrium became *more* compact, with a thicker myocardial wall and smaller chamber diameters. So the one model here that could in principle have shown a compaction defect showed the opposite.
